cds.text: Identify how curriculum texts are organised differently and use language features depending on purpose
Describe how curriculum texts use different language features and structures relevant to their purpose
Identify how texts have different language features and are typically organised into characteristic stages by purpose
Understand how texts are made cohesive through personal and possessive pronouns and omitting inferable words
Understand that paragraphs organise written texts by grouping related information together
Identify how connectives (temporal and conditional words) and topic word associations sequence and connect ideas
Navigate print and screen texts using chapters, contents, indexes, side-bar or drop-down menus, and links
Identify the purpose of layout features in print and digital texts, and the words used for navigation
Identify online text navigation features that enhance readability, such as headlines, drop-down menus, links, graphics and layout
Identify how similar topics and information are presented in different text types
Recognise how texts can share similar purposes but target different audiences
Compare texts from different times with similar purposes and audiences, noting differences in how events are depicted
Identify the purpose and audience of imaginative, informative and persuasive texts
Identify audience and purpose of these text types through language features and/or images
Identify characteristic features these text types use to meet their purpose
Read texts with phrasing and fluency using phonic and word knowledge, re-reading and self-correcting
Read a range of texts using phonic, semantic and grammatical knowledge, accurately and fluently, re-reading and self-correcting
Read different text types, integrating phonic, semantic and grammatical knowledge to read accurately and fluently
Use comprehension strategies, including monitoring, to build literal and inferred meaning
Use comprehension strategies while listening and viewing to build meaning, and begin evaluating texts
Use comprehension strategies, including monitoring, to build meaning, expand topic knowledge and evaluate texts
Manipulate more complex sounds in spoken words, using blending, segmenting, phoneme deletion and substitution to read and write words
Use short and common long vowels, consonant blends and digraphs to write and blend words; read consonant clusters and silent letters in words of one or more syllables, including compound words
Blend and segment to read and write multisyllabic words with more complex letter patterns fluently
Read and write words with more complex letter combinations, including a variety of vowel sounds and known prefixes and suffixes
Use spelling patterns and morphemes to read and write words not fully predictable from sounds, including high-frequency words
Apply common base words, prefixes, suffixes and suffix-adding generalisations to read and understand new multimorphemic words
Use letter patterns (including double letters), spelling generalisations, word families, prefixes, suffixes and word origins to spell more complex words
Build morphemic word families using knowledge of prefixes and suffixes
Use phoneme-grapheme relationships and less common letter patterns to spell words
Recognise and write most high-frequency words, including some homophones
Read and write high-frequency words, including homophones, and use context to identify correct spelling

sentences.text: {{S}} makes observations and supports them with evidence from the text to enhance {{pos}} understanding of stories and information.
{{S}} reads with confidence and uses context, grammar knowledge and skimming strategies to locate information in moderately complex texts.
{{S}} applies reading strategies to interpret complex texts and explains how these texts communicate meaning.
{{S}} monitors {{pos}} understanding and recognises when meaning breaks down.
{{S}} explains how authors make deliberate choices to shape the reader's perception.
{{S}} interprets key ideas in narratives and digital texts, and recognises how authors use language to shape meaning.
{{S}} comprehends digital texts and advertisements and identifies key ideas in narratives.
{{S}} identifies main ideas, understands simple inferences and explains how authors use evidence to support ideas.
{{S}} uses reading strategies to comprehend more complex texts.
{{S}} reads with confidence and uses skimming strategies to identify key ideas and locate details, and uses context to understand unfamiliar words.
{{S}} can interpret language features, explain how authors use evidence to support ideas and understands simple inferences when reading moderately complex texts.
{{S}} identifies main ideas and is beginning to recognise how language features help build meaning.
{{S}} is beginning to explain how language features, such as word choices and text clues, contribute to meaning.

{{S}} can interpret language features, explain how authors use evidence to support ideas and understands simple inferences when reading moderately complex texts.

rows.newText: {{S}} describes how texts use different language features and structures to suit their purpose.
{{S}} explains how a text is organised into characteristic stages that suit its purpose.
{{S}} identifies how language features change from one text type to another.
{{S}} explains how paragraphs group related information together in a written text.
{{S}} recognises that a new paragraph signals a change of idea.
{{S}} explains how time words and topic word links sequence ideas in a text.
{{S}} identifies words that show order and condition, such as first, then and if, when reading.
{{S}} identifies the purpose of headings, captions and layout in print and digital texts.
{{S}} uses the words and symbols that guide navigation in digital texts.
{{S}} uses headlines, menus and links to move through online texts and find information.
{{S}} explains how online navigation features make a text easier to read.
{{S}} recognises that texts with the same purpose can be aimed at different audiences.
{{S}} compares two texts with a similar purpose and explains how they suit different readers.
{{S}} compares texts from different times that share a purpose and notes how they differ.
{{S}} explains how the audience and purpose of a text affect the way it is written.
{{S}} identifies the audience and purpose of a text using its language features and images.
{{S}} explains how images and words work together to meet the purpose of a text.
{{S}} identifies the characteristic features that a text type uses to meet its purpose.
{{S}} compares the features of imaginative, informative and persuasive texts.
{{S}} reads a range of texts accurately and fluently using what {{s}} knows about sounds, meaning and grammar.
{{S}} reads aloud with expression and self-corrects when the meaning is unclear.
{{S}} reads different types of text accurately and fluently by combining phonic, meaning and grammar knowledge.
{{S}} adjusts {{pos}} reading speed and expression to suit different text types.
{{S}} uses comprehension strategies while reading to build meaning and begin to evaluate ideas.
{{S}} asks and answers questions about a text to build understanding.
{{S}} monitors understanding and uses comprehension strategies to expand {{pos}} topic knowledge.
{{S}} summarises key ideas from a text and links them to what {{s}} already knows.
